Plot the current parameter set against a candidate, for review

plot_growth_candidate.Rd

Both trajectories are drawn over the same references, with the fitting window shaded. This is the figure to look at when deciding whether a sweep result is worth promoting: it shows what actually changes, over the part of the curve the objective responds to.

Usage

plot_growth_candidate(
  species,
  current_curve,
  candidate_curve,
  reference,
  binned = NULL,
  current_label = "current parameters",
  candidate_label = "best candidate",
  x_max = 400,
  mature_window = c(100L, Inf),
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

species

Character. Modelled species code.

current_curve, candidate_curve

Tibbles with age and aboveground_c_mg_ha. candidate_curve may be NULL.

reference

A data frame of reference observations, with columns source ("SORTIE", "TIPSY" or "Ground plots"), age and aboveground_c_mg_ha.

binned

Optional tibble from growth_bin_observations().

current_label, candidate_label

Character legend labels.

x_max

Numeric. Upper age limit.

mature_window

Numeric length-2. Fitting window to shade.

subtitle

Character. Overrides the default subtitle.

Value

A ggplot.

Details

The age-binned plot series is drawn as well, in orange. That series – not the scatter behind it – is what the ground-plot term of the score is computed against, so a candidate that looks wrong against the cloud but right against the binned points is behaving exactly as scored.
